Troubleshooting

pdmS7 documentation

Source: vignettes/troubleshooting.Rmd
troubleshooting.Rmd

The common problems, the message pdmS7 gives, and what to do. Each message on this page is produced by the package itself when the site is built, so it matches what you will see.

Data

Missing or negative inputs 

says(run_pdm(model, data.frame(rain = c(1, NA), pet = 0.05)))
#> [1] "rain must contain finite nonnegative numbers"
says(run_pdm(model, data.frame(rain = c(1, 2), pet = c(0.05, -1))))
#> [1] "pet must contain finite nonnegative numbers"

The model cannot run through a gap in rain or PET, and negative values are data faults. Infill rain by one recorded method; fill PET from a seasonal curve. Preparing your data, steps 2, 5 and 6.

Rows that do not line up 

config <- pdm_presets("standard")
says(calibrate_pdm(config, forcing, observed = c(1, 2, 3), lower = c(fc = 0.8),
                   upper = c(fc = 1.2)))
#> [1] "observed length must match forcing"

The forcing and the observed flow must have one row each per time step. Join them on time, not by position, and fill missing time steps with explicit rows.

Scores that cannot be computed 

says(calibrate_pdm(config, forcing, observed = rep(2, 6), lower = c(fc = 0.8),
                   upper = c(fc = 1.2), objective = "nse"))
#> [1] "NSE needs variable observations"

NSE compares the model with the mean observed flow, so it needs flow that varies. A window that is almost all missing, or a constant flow, usually means the wrong file or a broken gauge record.

Times

If the model’s floods arrive one step early or late on every event, the rain or the flow is stamped at the start of the step instead of the end, or is in local time instead of UTC. Plot a few sharp storms: flow cannot rise before the rain that causes it.

Calibration

Bounds and starting values 

says(calibrate_pdm(config, forcing, observed = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1), lower = c(fc = 1.2),
                   upper = c(fc = 1.5)))
#> [1] "Initial parameters outside bounds"

The starting value of each calibrated parameter, from the configuration, must lie inside its bounds. Widen the bounds or change the starting configuration. calibration_bounds() gives default bounds that include the standard presets.

Parameters ending on a bound

Not an error, but a warning sign. The search was stopped by the fence, not by the data. Check the data first (wrong area, biased rainfall, a rating change), then consider whether the bound is physically justified. Widening a bound to let a parameter run away rarely gives a better model. The start_results table of a calibration shows each start’s final values.

Starts that disagree

Several starts ending at different parameters with similar scores mean the data do not pin those parameters down (equifinality). More starts will not fix it. Staged calibration (calibrate_staged()), which fits groups of parameters to the parts of the hydrograph they control, often helps. Automatic calibration, explained.

A threshold objective with the gradient method 

says(calibrate_pdm(config, forcing, observed = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1), lower = c(fc = 0.8),
                   upper = c(fc = 1.2), thresholds = c(alert = 2.5), method = "lbfgsb"))
#> [1] "Threshold scores change in steps, which a gradient optimiser cannot follow; use method = \"nelder_mead\" or \"dds\""

Threshold scores change in steps, so a gradient method cannot follow them. Use method = "nelder_mead".

The search found nothing valid

No valid calibration evaluation; inspect configuration and bounds means every trial failed to run. Usually a combination of components and bounds that the model rejects, for example demand recharge with a cascade groundwater store. Run the starting configuration once with run_pdm(): its error says what is wrong.

Model structure 

says(pdm_model(recharge = DemandRecharge(alpha = 0.5, beta = 1, qsat = 101)))
#> [1] "no error"
says(correct_state(pdm_model(td = 2), initial_state(pdm_model(td = 2)), 1))
#> [1] "State correction requires td=0; delayed observations need a lag-aware smoother"

Some components only make sense together. Demand recharge needs a single groundwater store with room for its rate; state correction needs no outlet delay (td = 0), because with a delay the latest observation reflects an earlier state. Choosing model components.

Batches

A basin failed

batch_status() shows the step it reached and the reason. Fix the cause, often a data file, and run the same calibrate_batch() call again: finished basins pass through in moments and the failed one carries on from where it stopped. Use only = "B06" to retry just that basin. Calibrating many catchments.

A lock left behind

If R was stopped while writing to a project, the next write may report removing a stale lock. That is expected: the package clears a lock left by a session that no longer exists.

The calibration log

Not enough years to hold back 

time <- seq(as.POSIXct("2020-10-01", tz = "UTC"), by = 86400, length.out = 3 * 365)
says(wettest_years(time, rep(1, length(time)), n = 2))
#> [1] "Only 3 water years have at least half a year of observed flow; holding back 2 would leave fewer than 3. Hold back fewer years, or none with 0"

By default register_data() holds back the two wettest water years, which needs a record of at least five years with half of each observed. For a shorter record, set wettest_years = 1 or 0 and say why in the registration’s reasoning. Without a time column in the forcing, registration refuses for the same reason: water years need dates. If holding back the wettest year leaves the validation window almost empty, lengthen the window; the message names it. Larger floods.

A data file has changed

Registered ... file has changed since registration means a data file no longer matches the checksum taken when it was registered. Someone edited or replaced it. Do not carry on: restore the original, or register the new file as new data with a note explaining why.

An entry no longer reproduces

... no longer reproduces its recorded output means rerunning a logged configuration gives a different flow. Usually the package or R has changed since the entry was written. verify_project(project, rerun = TRUE) names what changed. Recalibrate under the new version, or run the old version to reproduce the record.

A Steward cannot sign off 

sign_off_project(project, "Accepted.", reviewed)
#> Error: You wrote calibration entries in this project; another Steward must sign off

By design. A Steward who took part in the calibration cannot sign it off. Ask another Steward, or a Delegated Steward. Reviewing a calibration.

Forecasting 

says(pdm_hindcast(model, forcing, observed = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1), window = 6:6))
#> [1] "No forecast origins fit in the window"

A hindcast needs room for forecast origins inside the window, with at least one step after each. Widen the window or shorten every_h. Testing forecasts with hindcasts.

Still stuck

Check the function’s help page (?calibrate_pdm and so on), then the Glossary for any unfamiliar term. If the package itself seems wrong, report it with a small example that reproduces the problem on the issue tracker.
